correctness.rationale: For the finite irreducible fixed-k SSEP, the exact one-site second-difference potential lifts to a solution of the full interacting Poisson equation on the canonical configuration space. The centered integrated block occupation differs by a bounded corrector from a square-integrable martingale; its asymptotic variance equals the stationary bracket. Exact hypergeometric particle-vacancy occupancy gives w_i = 2k(n-k)d_i^2/[r n(n-1)]. Summing explicitly evaluated squared cycle gradients yields the claimed polynomial variance. Strict gradient inequalities identify the two unique dominant bonds, prove the 6m(n-m)/(n[m(n-m)+2]) fraction, and bound any K retained bonds by 3K/n. The n>=12 strict-majority cutoff and n=11,m=5 witness are direct exact consequences. The packaged standard-library script separately solves 94 full interacting configuration-space Poisson systems, 219 single-site Poisson systems, and 10098 edge weights. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the general proof. No statement beyond stated n,k,m,r boundaries is claimed.

value.rationale: The physically motivated measurable invariant is the zero-frequency variance of residence time in a contiguous block, important to low-frequency transport and noise-reduction fidelity. The exact theorem shows that the two unique best individual noise sources nevertheless have only 6/n of total variance asymptotically, independent of occupation density, and exhibits a sharp universal n=12 majority-loss threshold. All k and m are classified with a natural finite-volume correction, not arbitrary isolated parameter values. This distinguishes source ranking from fidelity with a fixed source budget. No general downstream theorem or thermodynamic transition is asserted.
